summary.text: A microscope is a laboratory instrument used to examine objects too small to be seen with the naked eye.
The most common type, and the first invented, is the optical microscope, which uses lenses to bend visible light passing through or reflecting off a sample.
Other major types include fluorescence microscopes, electron microscopes and scanning probe microscopes.

facts.label: Compound microscopes
facts.value: Appeared in Europe around 1620, inventor unknown

facts.label: Van Leeuwenhoek
facts.value: Reached up to 300 times magnification with one lens

facts.label: Micro-organisms
facts.value: Van Leeuwenhoek reported their discovery on 9 October 1676

facts.label: Kohler illumination
facts.value: Developed in 1893 to give even lighting

facts.label: First electron microscope
facts.value: A prototype built by Ruska and Knoll in 1931

items.prompt: A transmission electron microscope works on similar principles to a light microscope. What replaces the light and the glass lenses?

options.label: Sound waves and bowls of water
X-rays and flat mirrors
Heat and metal plates
Electrons and electromagnets

items.explain: It uses electrons in place of light and electromagnets in place of glass lenses.

items.prompt: What two parts does a compound microscope combine to give a viewer a real image?

options.label: An objective lens near the specimen and an eyepiece
A mirror near the eye and a lens near the lamp
Two eyepieces facing each other
A flat glass plate and a needle mount

items.explain: Compound microscopes combine an objective lens near the specimen with an eyepiece to view a real image.

items.prompt: Early microscopes gave dim, uneven views with poor contrast. What did Kohler illumination add?

options.label: A stronger lamp that made the specimen glow
Even lighting that overcame limited contrast and resolution
A second lens that doubled the magnification
A beam of electrons in place of light

items.explain: It gives even lighting and overcomes the limited contrast and resolution of early illumination methods.

items.prompt: A biologist wants to see a clear, transparent cell without staining it. Which developments made that possible?

options.label: Larger glass globule lenses on a stand
Adjustable needle mounts held with screws
Phase contrast and differential interference contrast
Brighter electric lamps as light sources

items.explain: Phase contrast and differential interference contrast illumination allow imaging of unstained, transparent samples.

items.prompt: What was unusual about Antonie van Leeuwenhoek's microscope?

options.label: It used a single tiny ball lens yet reached high magnification
It chained many lenses together in a long tube
It used a beam of electrons to light the specimen
It used a concave mirror to light the specimen

items.explain: He reached up to 300 times magnification with a simple single lens, a very small glass ball held between metal plates.

items.prompt: For a compound light microscope, which pair of parts mainly decides how good the image is?

options.label: The eyepiece and the stand
The focusing knob and the slide
The lamp and the table
The condenser system and the objective lens

items.explain: Performance depends on the condenser focusing light on the specimen and the objective capturing light to form an image.
